copy.title: Separating Model Reasoning from Physical Authority in Agentic Hardware Engineering
copy.abstract: Tool-using AI agents can move plausible model output toward fabrication or power-on before component identity, evidence provenance, revision state, or physical behavior is established. We present Hardware-Splicer, a model-independent environment that separates semantic agent reasoning from deterministic engineering constraints, provenance-bearing evidence, exact project state, and scoped human physical authority. General-purpose agents operate a canonical backend through the Model Context Protocol, while evidence and authority gates remain outside the model. A frozen ten-case adversarial SPI-flash corpus covers source-order perturbations, partial evidence, identity conflict, tool failure, plausible wrong analogy, and stale revision. Current evidence establishes the deterministic software and MCP infrastructure: real stdio and Streamable HTTP clients complete canonical stateful operations across a 193-operation backend while MCP remains unable to grant physical authority. Live external-model, fresh physical, and independent-operator results remain separate claims until those experiments run. The architecture therefore permits agent usefulness and permission to act to be evaluated as distinct outcomes.
nonclaims: Do not claim a live external model has passed the frozen corpus.
Do not claim fresh physical correctness evidence exists.
Do not claim independent-operator validation or production readiness.
Do not convert software/MCP verification into physical-action authority.
